analysis.answer: Current law does not address religious displays in public school classrooms. The measure requires every public school classroom to display a poster of the Ten Commandments that meets specific size and legibility requirements.
Direct costs include acquiring, printing, mounting, or framing the posters for every classroom in the public school system.
Local public schools and districts will bear the costs of purchasing and displaying the posters.

Because the text does not specify which translation or tradition's version of the Ten Commandments to use, school districts will have to select one. The measure is also likely to trigger constitutional litigation over the Establishment Clause, potentially delaying implementation and creating legal costs for the state.

The text addresses a perceived absence of foundational religious or historical texts in the educational environment by mandating their display. It does not contain a mechanism for funding the mandate.
State lawmakers gain control over classroom displays, reducing the discretion of local school boards, administrators, and individual teachers regarding what goes on their walls.
This is a statutory change that can be repealed by future legislation or blocked by a court ruling.

items.text: Expands religious expression in public institutions by requiring the Ten Commandments to be displayed in all public school classrooms.
